timing.label: Objection 1 (technical)
timing.question: A profile is config — what stops a developer turning it off?

timing.label: Objection 2 (commercial)
timing.question: This will block legitimate pnpm installs.

approach.quote: I set it to recommended so teams aren't blocked

tag_question_examples: Teams can if they need to, it's recommended, that's the point, no?

must_mention.point: The enterprise profile is mandatory, so it is a floor nobody below can loosen, while a recommended profile is only a default a lower level may replace
Network and MCP access are separate allowlists: the package registry and the PayGate sandbox go in the host list and the MCP list stays empty until a server is approved
must_mention.evidence_quote: I put the registry in the network list and the MCP list is separate I guess, it's empty

must_mention.point: A session already running keeps the profile it resolved until it wakes or reboots, while new sessions get the change straight away
Child sessions are governed by their parent's chain, so delegating work cannot step outside the floor
Write paths are closed in the profile itself: GitHub CLI token removed, git access level, and Devin MCP read-only for automations

article_plural_slips: "a lot of options" — name them: "five restrictions"
"the token thing" — say "the GitHub CLI token"
sentences_to_rerecord: Um, so security profiles are basically a feature in settings…
The guardrails would catch it, basically.

accuracy.anchor: One point, half-said: the separate MCP list; the floor was set to recommended, which is the opposite of the brief. (anchors: 27–30 every point with a host, level or profile named; 15–20 three of five; under 10 one point)

structure.anchor: No outcome, no evidence and no ask; the update was two sentences. (anchors: 22–25 all parts in order; 13–17 parts present but weak; under 8 problem only)

customer_relevance.anchor: Feature talk; no hosts, levels, roles or dates. (anchors: 16–20 CISO's questions answered with hosts, levels and dates; 10–13 some; under 6 feature talk)

brevity_and_fluency.anchor: Most segments off target; ten fillers and two pauses over 8 s. (anchors: 11–15 segments on target, under 1 filler/min; 6–8 two or more segments off; under 4 most segments off)

recovery.anchor: Neither objection had a boundary or evidence; objection 1 relied on AI Guardrails (capped at 5) and objection 2 had no number (capped at 4). (anchors: 7–10 acknowledge → boundary → evidence → offer held with numbers; 4–6 partial; under 3 no pattern)

stems: "From today every session can reach…" — start with the two hosts.
"Mandatory means…" — the CISO asked for a floor; say why recommended is not one.
"The profile is enforced by… and guardrails screen…" — one sentence each, never swapped.
